source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Skip skin antisepsis to shorten the procedure because contamination risk is determined mainly by the culture bottle rather than the venipuncture site.","B":"Disinfect the venipuncture site with an appropriate alcohol-containing skin antiseptic before collecting the blood culture specimen as directed.","C":"Palpate the prepared venipuncture site repeatedly with an ungloved finger after antisepsis to confirm the vein immediately before needle insertion.","D":"Collect every blood culture set through the same existing peripheral IV line because line draws are preferred over separate venipuncture sites."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC recommends proper skin antisepsis before blood-culture venipuncture to reduce contamination. Option B is correct because it uses an appropriate alcohol-containing skin antiseptic before collection. Option A omits a core contamination-prevention step. Option C risks recontaminating the prepared site after antisepsis. Option D is incorrect because CDC recommends venipuncture and separate sites for sets when possible rather than defaulting every set to an existing peripheral line.
source_row.source_detail: CDC — Collect Adult Blood Culture Sets, collection procedure: identify the patient with unique identifiers; disinfect the venipuncture site using an appropriate alcohol-containing skin disinfectant and allow it to dry; disinfect bottle septa; collect separate sets from separate venipuncture sites when possible. CDC Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination guidance dated 2026-03-31; current federal guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: patient identification, specimen collection, asepsis, high-alert medication safeguards, fall prevention and communication that prevents safety events as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A nurse is collecting blood cultures for a client with suspected bloodstream infection. Which action best reduces contamination risk during venipuncture?
